# Whether Painted or Papered, Muraled Walls Make Bold Statements in the Home


The ancient practice of covering walls in artistic scenery is back.


by[Trent Morse](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/contributors/trent-morse/)


[Pin](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/create/button/)


[Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/home-murals/)


[Tweet](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Whether%20Painted%20or%20Papered%2C%20Muraled%20Walls%20Make%20Bold%20Statements%20in%20the%20Home%20on%20The%20Study%3A%20The%20%401stDibs%20Blog&url=https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/home-murals/)


Email


Photo by Noe DeWitt


A South Asian fantasia envelops the living room of a sprawling[International-Style Dallas home](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/dallas-international-style-residence-dallas-tx/388042/) designed by[Redd Kaihoi](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/miles-redd/) . A[George II](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/george-ii/) carved-pickled-pine mirror and a 20th-century parcel-gilt mahogany-and-cane[coffee table](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/coffee-tables-cocktail-tables/) add to the spaces collected charm.


**“Believe it or not, the entire house was inspired by[Coco Chanel](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/chanel/fashion/) ,” says Miles Redd, who coheads the firm with David Kaihoi.**


Contrasting with the elaborateness are crisp white upholstery and a vintage cotton[dhurrie](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/indian-dhurrie/) with boating stripes make for “a very Chanel notion,” Redd adds. “The mural answers with all the ornate drama the rest of the room withholds, and the contrast is what makes the whole thing sing.”


---


Photo by Jared Kuzia


“Murals are a great way to bring visual interest and movement into a space. I love the way they make your eye travel around the room and create a sense of discovery,” says Melissa Sanabria, of[Sanabria & Co](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/melissa-sanabria-design/) .


In the dining room of a[1928 Colonial-style house in Chevy Chase, Maryland](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/chevy-chase-colonial-chevy-chase-md/442612/) , she paired[Charlotte Terrell](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/charlotte-terrell/) ’s ethereal For Fearless Virtue wallcovering by Area Environments with Farrow & Ball’s Beverly, a deep-green paint tone, on the ceiling, wainscoting, millwork and door.


A 1970s[Drexel](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/drexel/furniture/) walnut-parquetry table from 1stDibs, the clients’ own vintage chairs with custom[Cowtan & Tout](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/cowtan-and-tout/) cushions and a[Mahal rug](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/vintage-mahal-rug/) add to the room’s sense of historicity. Above it all, a Ruemmler silk pendant spices up the scene with a more contemporary flavor.


“When clients are in the early stages of building an art collection and don’t have much to hang on the walls,” Sanabria says, “a mural itself serves as the art piece.”


---


Photo by Kerri McCaffety


In the living room of an[1836 townhouse in New Orleans](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/french-quarter-apartment-new-orleans-la/7473/) ’s French Quarter,[Thomas Jayne](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/jayne-design-studio/) wrapped the walls in an undulating 19th-century-looking panorama of life on the Mighty Miss.


“We worked with[de Gournay](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/de-gournay/) to design a scenic paper based on C. H. DeWitt’s illustrations in one of my favorite childhood books, *The Story of the Mississippi* ,” Jayne says.


The custom creation also reflects the designer’s longtime interest in the landscape murals found in traditional Southern interiors of yore. A bright-blue dado and yellow trim pick up the wallcovering’s pastel palette while enhancing the room’s Creole character.


“Historic examples of scenic papers are typically drawn with the horizon line at one level,” Jayne says, “so the scene easily continues around the walls of the room.”


---


Photo by Stephen Karlisch


A glimmering[de Gournay](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/de-gournay/) wallcovering, stylized with gilded bas-relief details and depicting a big cat in a jungle setting, sets the scene in[Ken Fulk](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/ken-fulk/) ’s[study for a recent Kips Bay Decorator Show House in Dallas](https://www.1stdibs.com/1stdibs-50/2022/design-firm/ken-fulk-inc/) .


A dark-lacquered ceiling,[leopard-print club chairs](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/leopard-chairs/) and a[classical-inspired sculpture](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/decorative-objects/sculptures/style/classical-greek/) on a winged[Suë et Mare](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/sue-et-mare/) desk from Houston’s[Moxie Interiors](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/moxie/shop/) contribute to the[Art Nouveau](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/art-nouveau/) –meets–[Art Deco](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/art-deco/) ambience.


Part of a suite of lively rooms, the space reflects Fulk’s wish to convey what he calls “the feeling of a joyous reawakening after a long slumber.”


A dark lacquered ceiling,[leopard-print club chairs](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/leopard-chairs/) and a[classical-inspired sculpture](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/decorative-objects/sculptures/style/classical-greek/) atop a[Suë et Mare](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/sue-et-mare/) desk from Houston’s[Moxie Interiors](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/moxie/shop/) add to the layered feel.


To Fulk, the psychological resonance of a room matters as much as its visual appeal. “Beauty,” he says, “is very deeply entwined with what we have an emotional connection to.”


---


Photot by Blaine Davis


A monochrome menagerie of tropical animals cavorting among classical ruins fills the Shelley Reed mural above the sofa in a[Fifth Avenue pied-à-terre](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/pembrooke-and-ives-fifth-avenue/) by[Pembrooke & Ives](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/pembrooke-ives/) .


The painting followed the clients from their previous Manhattan apartment. “It had to be retrofitted for here,” says firm founder Andrew Sheinman. “We debated whether to cut off part of a monkey or a bird to fit the space.”


The couple ultimately found a way to accommodate the entire composition, reflecting their attachment to their quite personal art collection. A rubber credenza by[Brian Thoreen](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/brian-thoreen/furniture/) and a pair of[Edward Wormley](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/edward-wormley/furniture/) chairs continue the room’s eclectic mingling of contemporary and vintage design.


As for the color palette, “It’s very much to the wife’s taste,” says Stephanie Sarkies-Schabot, Pembrooke & Ives’s managing director. “She loves anything dark or jewel toned.”


---


Photo by Shade Degges


“It does go against the grain of what you expect,” says[Pamela Shamshiri](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/studio-shamshiri/) of the breakfast nook in a[1906 Southern California retreat](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/california-swiss-chalet-ojai-ca/76771/) she renovated for a Hollywood power couple.


The[English Country](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/english-country-house/) moment in a largely[chalet-style house](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/chalets/) comes courtesy of a Susan Harter wallcovering depicting the[Cotswolds](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/paintings-of-cotswold/) , unexpectedly installed between the battens above and below the windows.


At first, Shamshiri pondered a more traditionally scaled pattern but was won over by Harter’s tall trees, which “pull the view outside the windows into the room,”[she says](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/studio-shamshiri-home-tour/) .


Green trim and celadon-stained ceilings reinforce the verdant palette, while a custom banquette, a Springsteen table by Sawkille’s[Jonah Meyer](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/desks-writing-tables/craft-table-chair-jonah-meyer-1997/id-f_44857802/) , 1940s Italian[wood-and-leather chairs](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/leather-and-wood-chairs/) and small brass[Michael Anastassiades](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/michael-anastassiades/) pendants balance out all the green.


“It might be my favorite spot in the house,” the designer mentions. “The scale is so nice, and you sit surrounded by views from windows on three sides.”


---


Photo courtesy of Beata Heuman


Twin[canopy beds](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/canopy-beds/) give[Beata Heuman](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/beata-heuman-ltd/) ’s daughters a sense of individual territory in their shared bedroom in the family’s[London townhouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/riverside-townhouse--hammersmith-gb/132762/) .


But it’s the walls that turn the room into a world of its own: a wondrous scene of anthropomorphized rabbits inspired by[Ludwig Bemelmans](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/ludwig-bemelmans-1898-1962-american/art/) , the[Madeline creator](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/ludwig-bemelmans-coney-island/) whose murals are a fixture of Bemelmans Bar inside New York’s Ritz-Carlton hotel.


Heuman upholstered the headboards in her Palm Drop fabric in Sky Blue/Plaster, adding a botanical counterpoint to the playful imagery. The goal,[she says](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/upholstered-beds/) , was to concoct a room that would “evoke a fairy-tale feeling” and “spark the imagination of my two daughters.”


---


Photo by Gentl & Hyers


“White — a calming, cleansing absence of color — allows you to regroup and exhale, which is particularly important in New York,” says designer[Kelly Behun](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/kelly-behun-studio/) .


In her[Central Park West penthouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/central-park-modern-penthouse-new-york-ny/3463/) , that philosophy finds an expressive companion in a mural by artist Kara Hamilton, with its gentle cloudscape split by ethereal fissures as if the sky is opening to another dimension.


A pale[antler chandelier](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/material/antler/) , swathed in gauzy fabric, hangs above the dining table, which is met by cushy sofas of[Behun’s own design](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/kelly-behun-studio/furniture/) .


“I try to achieve a blend of high and low . . . and I like things to have space around them,”[she explains](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/kelly-behun/) . “For me, it’s about how a room makes you feel emotionally.”


---


Photo by Heather Talbert


In the dining room of a[family house in Highland Park, Illinois](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/north-shore-family-home-highland-park-il/209452/) ,[Wendy Labrum](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/wendylabrum/) introduced an inky, atmospheric mural to offset the[sun-drenched foyer](https://www.1stdibs.com/photo/modern-eclectic-entry-and-hall-highland-park-il/5586562/) .


“This new-construction home is light and bright,” she says, “and since the dining room sits right off the airy entryway, we wanted something a little moodier to set the tone for the adjacent[black-lacquered bar](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/black-lacquer-bars/) .”


The custom wallcovering by A New Wall depicts a landscape of rolling hills and grazing bovines. “It was the starting point for this room,” Labrum says, “and everything else evolved organically around it.”


The custom marble-topped dining table was inspired by a smaller antique piece. A[vintage cabinet](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/storage-case-pieces/cabinets/) and[rustic pottery](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/dining-entertaining/pottery/style/rustic/) provide character and depth. “When you have a defined space that can handle a wallpaper or painted mural,” Labrum says, “it’s a great way to make the space feel unique and special.”


---


Photo by Jacob Snavely


Murals feature prominently throughout a[tailored apartment on Manhattan’s Upper West Side](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/nyc-art-collectors-haven-new-york-ny/387782/) designed by Kristine Irving, of[Koo de Kir Architectural Interiors](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/koo-de-kir/) , for a family of Boston transplants eager for a fresh start. “They wanted a full about-face in decor and design,” Irving says, “and we created a colorful haven full of pattern and texture.”


In the[powder room](https://www.1stdibs.com/photo/contemporary-eclectic-organic-modern-bathroom-new-york-ny/9595102/) , hand-painted panels by[Porter Teleo](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/porter-teleo/) cover the walls in an earthy abstraction. The demilune silhouette of an Ochre[leather-wrapped console table](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/console-tables/material/leather/) echoes the panels’ curves. “Sometimes, a wall mural is all the room needs,” Irving says, “like being enveloped in a giant pattern hug.”


A similar visual language reappears in the office and guest room, where Porter Teleo’s hand-painted work continues across the ceiling above a custom[Murphy bed](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/murphy-bed/) by Koo de Kir. The multiuse space is further outfitted with bespoke desks, a[Lasvit pendant](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/lasvit-pendants/) and a[Serge Mouille floor lamp](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/serge-mouille/furniture/lighting/floor-lamps/) from 1stDibs. The presence of a[Ruth Bader Ginsburg portrait](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/ruth-bader-ginsburg-art/) by June August epitomizes the eclectic tastes of the art-collecting residents.


“We kept layering in more patterns,” Irving says, “and offered surprise moments like the Melin Tregwynt patterned blanket when the bed is pulled down.”


---


Photo by Jeff Hirsch


In the library of[her Manhattan apartment](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/east-side-apartment/78781/) , Janine Carendi MacMurray, founder of[Area Interior Design](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/area-interior-design/) , coated the paneled walls in high-gloss navy[lacquer](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/material/lacquer/) , then installed a hand-painted mural around the fireplace.


“I wanted to create a moment of impact in a room where the architecture offered only one small wall for expression,” she says. “That limitation became an opportunity.” The scene of delicate white branches and birds offers a peaceful pause within the room’s moody shell. “The mural is by[Gracie](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/gracie/furniture/) — a favorite of mine — chosen for its timeless elegance and the way it anchors the space.”


The furniture strikes a balance between refinement and function: A[French mid-century](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/french-mid-century-modern/)[brass coffee table](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/coffee-tables-cocktail-tables/material/brass/) , custom[Schumacher](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/schumacher/shop/) -upholstered sofa and[Lawson-Fenning](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/lawson-fenning/furniture/) chairs sit atop a herringbone[hide rug](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/rugs-carpets/material/hide/) . “Beauty and real life can — and should — coexist,” MacMurray says. “This room may seem delicate, but it has also hosted many lively[knee-hockey games](https://ustha.com/what-is-knee-hockey/) with my son and his friends.”


---


Photo by Pernille Loof


In the dining room of[Wesley Moon](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/wesley-moon/) ’s 1,750-square-foot[Manhattan apartment](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/designers-own-home-new-york-ny/277122/) , a hand-painted mural presents a fantastical counterpoint to the urban view outside.


Devised in collaboration with[de Gournay](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/de-gournay/) , the​ customized Scenes of Sicily​ dreamscape depicts Palermo’s Church of Maria Santissima del Carmelo​ surrounded by​ stylized vegetation, water, mountains and glowing sky, rendered in matte pigments over gold leaf.


“I have a love of history and travel, which were the inspirations for the design of my home,”[Moon says](https://www.1stdibs.com/blogs/the-study/interior-designers-homes/) . A curving[banquette](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/banquette-seating-for-sale/) — based on one Moon admired in a Parisian brasserie — offers cushy seating for guests beneath an opulent[ceramic chandelier](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/material/ceramic/) designed by Eve Kaplan to hold either bulbs or candles.


“I’m always trying to figure out what the contemporary version of something classical is,” Moon explains, “so I can get that old-world feeling but adjusted to modern times.”


---


Photo by Rodger Davies


Amy Kehoe, cofounder of[Nickey Kehoe](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/nickey-kehoe-design/) , designed this[home office in California’s Santa Monica Mountains](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/santa-monica-mountains/92123/) as a place of calm and separation. “The room is at the far end of the house, allowing for inherent peace,” she says. “The idea was to play into the serenity.”


A[sepia-tone](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/sepia-tone/) pastoral wallpaper by Susan Harter, with fading trees and soft groundcover, creates an immersive environment. A wooden desk by[Lawson-Fenning](https://www.1stdibs.com/dealers/lawson-fenning/) is paired with a Summer Studio lamp in a matching finish. A Nickey Kehoe credenza lines one wall, topped with a vintage brass-and-leather lamp by[Einar Backstrom](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/einar-backstrom/furniture/) . The brick flooring adds an outdoor-patio vibe.


“With anything bold,” Kehoe says, “we ask ourselves a series of questions: Does the expression feel dynamic and signature, or does it interrupt the home’s atmosphere?” In this case, the mural functions not as an exclamation mark but as a gentle wash of emotion meant to produce tranquility.


---


Photo by Brittany Ambridge


In a 1907[Edwardian house in San Francisco](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/rainbow-house-san-francisco-ca/381442/) ,[Noz Nozawa](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/noz-design/) conjured what she calls a “big wow” with a spectrum-spanning scheme in the entry that sets the tone for the rest of the home. A rainbow stair runner by Stark cascades from scarlet to lavender, culminating in a purple cut-to-fit pool-shaped rug on the ground floor.


Joining the riot of color are hand-painted murals by Caroline Lizarraga, which transfer the rug’s sense of fluidity onto the walls. Three geode-inspired forms— rendered in pink, red, orange and turquoise, with gold veining rippling across the surfaces — create a painterly tension with the home’s traditional millwork.


“A part of me wanted to tone down that grandeur,”[Nozawa says](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/noz-design/) . “By disobeying the architecture and softening lines, I knew we could knock it down a bit.”


A blue-globed[Murano-glass](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/lighting/chandeliers-pendant-lights/material/murano-glass/) chandelier, hanging like a jewel from the ceiling, is echoed by a[Jonathan Adler​](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/jonathan-adler/furniture/)[Globo console](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/console-tables/globo-console/id-f_8691393/) beneath the stained-glass bay window. “Nothing in our portfolio looks quite like it,” Nozawa says of her design for the foyer, and for the house as a whole.


---


Photo by Mali Azima


“This[Atlanta home was built in the 1930s](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/classic-chic-atlanta-ga/218982/) , and for the bathroom, we wanted to honor its[Regency-era roots](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/regency/) while giving it a fresh, modern twist,”[Melanie Turner](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/melanie-turner-interiors/) says of a jewel-box powder room in a lively project full of color. Working with architect Yong Pak, Turner created a space that balances ornate detail with contemporary effortlessness.


A hand-painted chinoiserie mural by Penshaw Hill envelops the room in black and gold. A vintage[brass-and-velvet chair](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/brass-armchair-with-velvet/) along with a[Waterworks](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/waterworks/furniture/) sink and fittings have appropriately trad forms in modern-day finishes, while a crisp[round mirror](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/round-mirror/) and Jiun Ho pendants present more[Space Age](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/space-age/) silhouettes. Still, everything plays nicely within the color scheme.


“We love using murals — especially in smaller rooms — because they instantly give the space a sense of drama and story,” Turner explains. “A mural can transport you, make the room feel layered and soulful and give even the tiniest powder room or hallway a bold, unforgettable personality.”


---


Photo by Rikki Snyder


In the dining room of a[sprawling traditional house in Manhasset](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/manhasset-home-manhasset-ny/325412/) , New York,[Hilary Matt](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/hilary-matt-interiors/) served up a bold, playful aesthetic, using a royal-blue botanical wallpaper by[de Gournay](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/de-gournay/) filled with graphic white branches and vibrant birds.


“This client wanted a fun and colorful pop when you walked into her home,” Matt says. “We loved the idea of doing a colorful and whimsical space.” Continuing the organic theme is a[live-edge dining table](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/live-edge-dining-tables/) , surrounded by brass-legged[Gubi Beetle](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/gubi-beetle-chair/) chairs upholstered in ocher velvet.


Above, a[Lindsey Adelman](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/lindsey-adelman/furniture/) branching globe fixture in brass picks up the chairs’ warm metal tones, while its armature advances the visual rhythm of the wallpaper. A tan[Stark rug](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/stark-rugs/) produces a soft shift in texture and hue underfoot.


---


Photo by Jeff Herr


“I envisioned this bedroom as a peaceful, collected escape — inviting and relaxed, with a thoughtful blend of vintage and modern elements,” says[Charlotte Lucas](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/charlottelucas/) , who layered the boudoir of a saucy[Atlanta poolhouse](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/a-little-slice-of-heaven-atlanta-ga/305372/) with color, texture and personality.


The whimsical House of Harris wallpaper features trees magically blooming with yellow, pink and periwinkle flowers and populated by brightly plumed birds, all on a white ground.


Reinforcing the room’s charm are bespoke furnishings and curated vintage finds: a custom bed in a[Claremont fabric](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/seating/swivel-chairs/swivel-chair-reupholstered-claremont-fabric/id-f_36558542/) with Samuel & Sons trim, a[Paavo Tynell](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/paavo-tynell/furniture/) floral chandelier, a plaid[Edward Wormley](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/edward-wormley/furniture/) bench and a bedside globe pendant suspended from long brass tubes, which was sourced from 1stDibs.


“I love using expressive walls to bring a little personality and playfulness into a space,” Lucas says. “It’s an easy way to set the tone for a room and make it feel layered and unique without being too serious.”


---


Photo by Jenn Verrier Photography


---


“A series of antique hand-painted[chinoiserie](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/style/chinoiserie/) murals was the original point of inspiration in this space,”[Corey Damen Jenkins](https://www.1stdibs.com/design-firms/corey-damen-jenkins-and-associates/projects/) says of this parlor in a[traditional home on Maryland’s Eastern Shore](https://www.1stdibs.com/1stdibs-50/2025/design-firm/corey-damen-jenkins-and-associates/) ​. “The entire color palette was informed by these panels.”


The interior​,[featured in this year’s 1stDibs 50](https://www.1stdibs.com/1stdibs-50/2025/design-firm/corey-damen-jenkins-and-associates/) , was designed for multiple functions​ —​ playing games, reading, noshing and lounging​ —​ with distinct furniture arrangements.


A[19th-century English library table](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/19th-century-library-table/) is paired with[spoon-back armchairs](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/spoon-back-chair/) by[Dessin Fournir](https://www.1stdibs.com/creators/dessin-fournir/) , while a Syrian[Moorish tray table](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/tray-tables/style/moorish/) ​ from 1stDibs anchors a more relaxed sitting area near the[fireplace](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/building-garden/fireplaces-mantels/) .


“Although very traditional in style,” the designer says, “this room is certainly not lacking personality or a distinct point of view.”


Period details, like a[Regency-style convex mirror](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/mirrors/convex-mirrors/style/regency/) and a knight-themed[18th-century secretary](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/storage-case-pieces/secretaires/period/18th-century/) , mingle with clean-lined club chairs, also by Dessin Fournir, and sleek[brass desk lamps](https://www.1stdibs.com/buy/vintage-brass-desk-lamp/) , creating what Jenkins calls “a wonderful tension point between antiquity and modernity.”
